transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

When there’s a line or a process, I just can’t seem to wait my turn without jumping ahead or changing plans, and it keeps messing up our money and appointments. It has gotten so bad lately that we almost got evicted, so my wife and our parish priest urged me to finally come in and get some help.
Have these difficulties with impatience and acting on impulse been a constant struggle for you since childhood, or do they seem to come and go in distinct phases?

It has been a constant struggle since I was a kid; back in elementary school, my teachers were always calling my mom because I couldn't stay in my seat and kept blurting things out. But it has become a really severe problem over the last two years since I had to start managing our family's tight budget and paperwork.
Do you often experience sudden, intense shifts in your mood, or do you find that your relationships with family and friends are very unstable and stormy?

No, I don't really have those sudden mood shifts or stormy relationships. My family and my priest are actually very supportive of me, and I'm mostly just anxious and stressed about trying to provide for them.
Along with the impulsivity, do you also struggle with sustaining your attention on tasks, frequently getting distracted, or losing track of important paperwork and details?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. When I try to focus on bills or assistance forms, my mind drifts off to the birds outside or a song in my head within a few minutes, forcing me to constantly restart. Also, trying to organize paperwork or plan my week makes me feel completely lost, which often leads to me forgetting important deadlines for turning in forms.
Besides the difficulty waiting in lines, do you currently struggle with physical restlessness, like fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or feeling a constant inner urge to stay on the move?

Yes, my legs are always bouncing and my fingers are constantly tapping on tables or my Bible when I'm in church. I get this buzzing feeling inside like I'm trapped if I try to sit still, so I often have to get up and pace around, even in waiting rooms where I might lose my spot.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets the full clinical criteria for F90.0 (Disturbance of activity and attention / ADHD, combined type). He has a clear history of both inattentive symptoms (distractibility, disorganization, forgetfulness) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (restlessness, pacing, inability to wait turn) that began in childhood and cause severe, multi-setting impairment in adulthood (financial distress, near eviction). Other differentials, such as personality disorders or primary mood disorders, have been ruled out. Therefore, the diagnosis is confirmed.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a chronic, lifelong history of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity dating back to childhood (elementary school). He meets the diagnostic criteria for Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ICD-10 F90.0: Disturbance of activity and attention) as evidenced by significant inattentive symptoms (difficulty sustaining focus, organization issues, forgetting deadlines) and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (fidgeting, inability to remain seated, inner restlessness, and difficulty waiting his turn). These symptoms cause severe functional impairment, including financial difficulties and near-eviction.
